evidence_items.publisher: Benton Institute (excerpting The New York Times)

receipt.public_excerpt: Free and easy to use, A.I. tools have generated a flood of fake photos and videos of candidates or supporters saying things they did not or appearing in places they were not—all spread with the relative impunity of anonymity online.

evidence_items.explanation: The NYT reports a flood of AI-made fake media of candidates in elections up to June 2025.

evidence_items.publisher: Oman Observer (syndicating The New York Times)

receipt.public_excerpt: In the unusually concentrated wave of elections that took place in 2024, AI was used in more than 80%, according to the International Panel on the Information Environment, an independent organisation of scientists based in Switzerland. It documented 215 instances of AI in elections that year

evidence_items.explanation: An independent panel found AI used in over 80% of 2024 elections worldwide, and the article says it played a harmful role in 69% of cases. That puts AI misinformation on the world stage.

evidence_items.publisher: Oman Observer (syndicating The New York Times)

receipt.public_excerpt: In Romania, a Russian influence operation using AI tainted the first round of last year’s presidential election, according to government officials. A court there nullified that result, forcing a new vote last month and bringing a new wave of fabrications.

evidence_items.explanation: A concrete international case. Officials said an AI-enabled foreign influence operation tainted a national election, and a court annulled the result.

receipt.public_excerpt: But if you skip the headline and read the piece itself, you’ll find a really useful catalog of some of the ways in which AI has been used in recent elections, with embedded multimedia examples.

evidence_items.explanation: An election law expert calls the headline exaggerated but says the article catalogs real AI uses in elections. That supports the narrower 'starting to see' claim, not a strong reading of 'wearing down democracy'.

unresolved_gaps: Research finding no conclusive evidence that AI changed 2024 election outcomes, by the Alan Turing Institute's CETaS, could not be read directly. It bears on impact, not on presence.
The original nytimes.com page was not read; a syndicated copy was used.
